messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: sim problem with indDist argument!
parts:
The error occurs on line 753 of the source code sim.R, in a hidden function called runRep(), which runs a single replication within the sim() function.  

implied <- fitted(attr(data, "fit"))

The problem occurs when trying to extract model-implied moments from a lavaan object which has not actually been fitted.  In this case, the fitted() method returns the error you see, but using lavInspect(fit, "cov.ov") and lavInspect(fit, "mean.ov") would return the needed information, although in a different format.  I'm not sure if the fitted() method used to work and something recently changed in lavaan, but I submitted a bug report on simsem's github site, with a link to this thread.

Until it gets fixed, I think you can get around the problem by using LISREL matrices (which I think is a safer method anyway) instead of lavaan syntax to specify your models.  See the first example on the ?model help page for syntax that is similar to your lavaan syntax.

loading <- matrix(0, 6, 2)
loading[1:3, 1] <- NA
loading[4:6, 2] <- NA
LY <- bind(loading, 0.7)

latent.cor <- matrix(NA, 2, 2)
diag(latent.cor) <- 1
RPS <- binds(latent.cor, 0.5)

TE <- binds(diag(NA, nrow = 6), diag(.51, nrow = 6))

CFA.Model <- model(LY = LY, RPS = RPS, TE = TE, modelType = "CFA")

dist2 <- bindDist(skewness = seq(-3, 3, length.out=6), kurtosis = seq(2, 5, length.out=6))
summary(dist2)

Output <- sim(5, model=CFA.Model, n=150, indDist = dist2)

This works.  Granted, this example assumes the population and analysis models are the same, like in your example.  But it also works if you have a different analysis model (e.g., a 1-factor model):

LY.an <- bind(matrix(NA, 6, 1), 0.7)
PS.an <- binds(matrix(1, 1, 1), 1)
analysisModel <- model(LY = LY.an, PS = PS.an, TE = TE, modelType = "CFA")
Output2 <- sim(5, model = analysisModel, generate=CFA.Model, n=150, indDist = dist2)

Hope this is sufficient to keep your study going.  Good luck!

Terry

messages.subject: Re: sim problem with indDist argument!
parts:
Hi, 

I am sorry for being late. As Terry said, this is a bug. Another way to work around it is to adjust the generate argument in the sim function, which may be easier.

popModel <- "
f1 =~ 0.7*y1 + 0.7*y2 + 0.7*y3
f2 =~ 0.7*y4 + 0.7*y5 + 0.7*y6
f1 ~~ 1*f1
f2 ~~ 1*f2
f1 ~~ 0.5*f2
y1 ~~ 0.49*y1
y2 ~~ 0.49*y2
y3 ~~ 0.49*y3
y4 ~~ 0.49*y4
y5 ~~ 0.49*y5
y6 ~~ 0.49*y6
"

analysisModel <- "
f1 =~ y1 + y2 + y3
f2 =~ y4 + y5 + y6
f1 ~~ 1*f1
f2 ~~ 1*f2
f1 ~~ f2
y1 ~~ y1
y2 ~~ y2
y3 ~~ y3
y4 ~~ y4
y5 ~~ y5
y6 ~~ y6
"

Output <- sim(5, model=analysisModel, n=150, generate=list(model = popModel, skewness = seq(-3, 3, length.out=6), kurtosis = seq(2, 5, length.out=6)), std.lv=TRUE, lavaanfun = "cfa")
summary(Output)

Best,
Sunthud
